html:
George Washington led the American army in the War of Independence and was the first president of the United States, from 1789 to 1797.

Born into a planter family in colonial Virginia, he first saw war as a young officer in the French and Indian War of the 1750s. He became a wealthy planter at Mount Vernon, which, like most large Virginian estates, was worked by enslaved people, and he sat in Virginia's elected assembly.

When the American Revolutionary War began in 1775, the Continental Congress made him commander of its army. He lost more battles than he won, but he kept a poorly supplied army in being through hard winters. He won small but vital victories at Trenton and Princeton in 1776 and 1777, and with French help he trapped the main British army at Yorktown in 1781, which ended the fighting.

His choices after the war mattered as much as his victories:

  • In 1783 he resigned his command and went home, rather than take power.
  • He presided over the convention that wrote the Constitution in 1787.
  • As president he built the new government, with Thomas Jefferson and Alexander Hamilton in his cabinet, and kept the country out of the wars of the French Revolution.
  • He stepped down after two terms, setting an example that held until 1940.

In his will he freed the enslaved people he owned outright, to take effect after his wife's death. He is still called the "Father of His Country".
sum: George Washington led the American army in the War of Independence and was the first president of the United States, from 1789 to 1797.
